Criminal Case No. 51286 of 2025

Ansh
 Versus
 Directorate Of Enforcement
 Appearance:
Shri Vishal Baheti, Senior Advocate with Shri Sahaj C  learned counsel for the applicant.
Shri Sunil Kumar Jain, Senior Advocate/AAG with Shri   Dave, Assistant Solicitor General, learned counsel for the re  ORDER 1.
They are heard.
Perused the case diary / challan papers.

2. This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (439 of Cr.P.C.) as he/she is implicated in connection with Crime No.
ECIR/INSZO/05/2024 registered at / by Directorate of Enforcement, Indore, District Indore (MP)
for offence punishable under Section 3 and 4 of Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and Scheduled Offence under Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 and Section 420, 467 and 471 of IPC, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 03/10/2025.

3. The allegation against the applicant is of his involvement in the aforesaid case registered under the provisions of Prevention of Money NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37628 2 MCRC-51286-2025 Laundering Act, involving evasion of state excise duty in issuance of liquor transport permit and challans.
4.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned senior counsel appearing for the applicant has submitted that the case was initially registered at Crime No.172/2017 at police station Raoji Bazar, Indore, in which, this Court was pleased to allow the application in M.Cr.C. No.8294/2018 dated 01/05/2018, however, the applicant Ansh vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76222234/
1 was also directed to deposit a sum of 1 Crore in the trial Court within a week's time and pursuant to which, the applicant has also deposited the same in the form of a fixed deposit in Union Bank of India, copy of which is also filed on record.

It is submitted that merely because subsequently the case has been handed over to the Enforcement Directorate, it would not be justified to arrest the applicant merely because the change in investigating agency, especially when he has already complied with the order passed by this Court and was enjoying liberty since 2018, and there is no allegation that the applicant misused the liberty extended to him.
Counsel has also submitted that the respondents have not challenged the order passed by this Court before the Supreme Court and thus, the applicant deserves to be released on bail.

5. Shri Sunil Jain, learned senior advocate/Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondent, on the other hand has vehemently opposed the prayer on the ground that merely because the applicant has been granted bail in the predicate offence, he cannot claim the bail under the provisions of Prevention of Money Laundering Act as a matter of right, and the conditions as imposed under Section 45(1) of the Act of 2002 have to be NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:37628 3 MCRC-51286-2025 satisfied while considering his bail application.
Shri Jain has also relied upon various judgments of the Supreme Court.

It is submitted that the applicant was managing the business of liquor at Sanwer, Dharampuri, Pigdumber area, and using his employees as proxies, forged challans were submitted through liquor shops under his ownership,
enabling the illegal procurement of liquor stock and evasion of duty, and the amount illegally generated by the applicant was also used to pay bribes to the officials of the State Excise Department and applicant's various assets have also been attached.
Hence, it is submitted that the application be dismissed.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary as also the documents filed on record.
7.

Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the documents filed on record, and the reply filed by the respondents, it is found that so far as the order passed by this Court in M.Cr.C. No.8294/2018 dated 01/05/2018 is concerned, the same cannot be relied upon by the applicant as now his application is strictly governed by the provisions of Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, and the order passed by this Court in his earlier bail application is of no avail to him.

8. So far as the allegations against the applicant are concerned, it is alleged that the applicant along with other co-accused manipulated the government records and have caused loss to the State exchequer to the tune of Rs.49,42,45,615/- crores.
It is also alleged that liquor licenses were also obtained for Dharampuri and Sanwer liquor groups in the name of his employees for tender period 2015-2016.

This court is of the considered NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:37628 4 MCRC-51286-2025 opinion that the applicant cannot hide behind his employees' names as they must be acting under his instructions only as he was the only one who stood beneficiary of his employees' actions, who were only his salaried employees.
Ansh vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76222234/
2 9.

It is also found that in the impugned order, the learned Judge of the trial Court has also referred to the involvement of total amount of defalcation to the tune of Rs.70 Crores, and this Court also finds that under the facts and circumstances, of the case, no such reasonable grounds exists to believe that the applicant is not guilty of the offence or that he is not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
In such circumstances, the application sans merits, is hereby dismissed.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE krjoshi Ansh vs Directorate Of Enforcement on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76222234/
